text:
sam: FYI — terraform apply in eu-central failed after bumping infra-modules/compute -> v2.5.0. The new module API made `fleet_tier` a required argument and planner wants to replace subnets.
jess: ouch. did plan show replacements or just an error?
sam: Plan showed replacements for aws_subnet.* and aws_network_interface.* then errored with missing arg.
sam: Error snippet:
```
Error: Missing required argument
  on modules/compute/main.tf line 42, in resource "aws_subnet" "worker":
  42: resource "aws_subnet" "worker" {

The argument "fleet_tier" is required, but no definition was found.
```
marta: that module was merged without a compatibility migration step? :eyes:
kai: Looks like PR author removed the default to force consumers to pick tier. But we have ~40 stacks that reference the module without passing fleet_tier.
oliver: We should avoid replacing subnets in prod. Suggest: pin prod branch to infra-modules/compute@v2.4.3, then ship a minor patch v2.4.4 that adds a soft default or optional param to avoid replacements.
jess: +1. Also add a CI preflight to detect new required args in modules (compare published module schema vs live module usage).
infra-bot: Created issue #452: "module change introduces required param `fleet_tier` -> causing resource replacement risk" (assign: @oliver)
deploy-bot: CI: https://ci.redwood/d/infra/plan/887 failed — exit 1
sam: I can open the revert pin PR for prod today. after that we coordinate a staged rollout for a patched module.
oliver: Opening PR now to pin infra repo (link: https://github.com/redwood/infrastructure/pull/1234) — includes temp pin to v2.4.3 and a tf-validate job.
kai: We should also run `terraform state list` across workspaces to ensure no drift hidden by imports. If anyone has transient subnets, replacing could move IPs and break node affinity.
marta: Ops concern: if subnets are recreated in eu-central, capacity allocations in that region are tight — replacements could trigger AZ fallback and autoscaler thrash.
sam: Action items:
- oliver: merge pin PR to unblock deploys (prod & staging) — today
- module owners: publish v2.4.4 patch that reintroduces optional fleet_tier with default, add migration docs — tomorrow
- devex: add module-API-change preflight CI check (fail PRs that add required args) — next sprint
- kai/marta: run spot-check `terraform state list` in eu-central workspaces and report resources that would be replaced — ASAP
jess: we should also add a GitOps gate: block Argo sync if module version bump modifies critical networking resources (subnet, route_table). small policy in repo-ci.
oliver: noted. I'll add a terraform-plan-parser hook that flags "replace" on aws_subnet and posts in PR.
sam: thanks all. once pin is merged i'll re-run applies in staging and run the drift checklist.
infra-bot: Reminder scheduled — weekly infra-module-audit job will include module contract diff report starting next week.
marta: FYI cost note: if we end up recreating subnets and reattaching ENIs, there may be short term egress and NAT gateway allocation costs. keep finance in loop if we hit replacements.
jess: ok closing loop here, update this thread when PR merged.
